'''Shoon Kyung Kim''' ({{langx|ko|김순경}}, 29 February 1920 – 14 March 2003) was a South Korean theoretical chemist whose work systematized [[Molecular symmetry|symmetry]] and [[Representation theory|representation theory]] for molecular and crystalline systems. He held faculty posts at [[Seoul National University]] (1951–1965), the [[University of Louisville]] (1966–1969), and [[Temple University]] (1969–1990).<ref name="KAST">{{cite web |title=(Late) Kim Shoon-kyung |url=https://www.koreascientists.kr/eng/merit/merit-list/?cntId=4&mode=view |website=Persons of Distinguished Service to Science and Technology (KAST) |publisher=Korean Academy of Science and Technology |date=3 February 2020 |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref> He authored the Cambridge monograph ''Group Theoretical Methods and Applications to Molecules and Crystals'' (1999).<ref name="CUP">{{cite book |last=Kim |first=Shoon K. |title=Group Theoretical Methods and Applications to Molecules and Crystals |year=1999 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-64062-6 |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511534867 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/group-theoretical-methods-and-applications-to-molecules-and-crystals/1F263CD2D65A120131230A0B9D80DF40 |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

Kim was the founding president (1972) of the [[Korean-American Scientists and Engineers Association]] (KSEA).<ref name="KSEA1">{{cite web |title=Inauguration |url=https://history.ksea.org/key-history/inauguration |website=KSEA History |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref><ref name="KSEA2">{{cite web |title=Short Bio and Photos — Presidents |url=https://history.ksea.org/presidents/short-bio-and-photos |website=KSEA History |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

== Education ==
Kim earned a B.S. in chemistry from [[Osaka University]] (1944) and a Ph.D. in chemistry from [[Yale University]] (1956).<ref name="KAST" /> At Yale he studied electrolyte theory under [[Lars Onsager]].<ref name="KAST" />

== Career ==
After early research posts in Japan and Korea, Kim joined the chemistry faculty at [[Seoul National University]] in 1949, serving there until 1965; he was a visiting professor at [[Brown University]] (1962–1966). He moved to the [[University of Louisville]] (1966–1969) and then to [[Temple University]] (1969–1990), later serving as honorary professor until his death in 2003.<ref name="KAST" /> He organized KSEA in late 1971 and served as its first president in 1972.<ref name="KSEA1" /><ref name="KSEA2" />

== Research and publications ==
Kim worked across statistical dynamics, [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemistry]], and [[Chemical physics|chemical physics]], publishing more than 70 papers and several books and translations.<ref name="KAST" /> His Cambridge monograph treats point and space groups (including [[Corepresentations of unitary and antiunitary groups|anti-unitary co-representations]]) with explicit constructions;<ref name="CUP" /> it received an independent review in ''Acta Crystallographica Section A'' assessing its approach to symmetry and applications in molecular vibrations and band theory.<ref name="ActaA">{{cite journal |last=Brock |first=C. P. |year=2000 |title=Review of ''Group Theoretical Methods and Applications to Molecules and Crystals'' |journal=Acta Crystallographica Section A |volume=56 |issue=4 |pages=550–551 |url=https://journals.iucr.org/a/issues/2000/04/00/by0195/by0195.pdf |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref> Earlier, Kim introduced a correspondence-theorem method for constructing symmetry-adapted linear combinations ([[Linear combination of atomic orbitals|SALCs]]) and symmetry coordinates.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Kim |first=Shoon K. |title=A new method of constructing symmetry-adapted linear combinations for a finite group. II. Correspondence theorem and basis operators |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications |volume=106 |issue=3 |year=1981 |pages=521–538 |doi=10.1016/0378-4371(81)90124-2 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0378437181901242 |access-date=29 October 2025|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Kim |first=Shoon K. |title=A new method of constructing the symmetry coordinates of molecular vibrations |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |volume=22 |issue=10 |year=1981 |pages=2303–2310 |doi=10.1063/1.524766 |url=https://pubs.aip.org/aip/jmp/article/22/10/2303/226090/A-new-method-of-constructing-the-symmetry |access-date=29 October 2025|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Honors ==
Kim was designated a “Person of Distinguished Service to Science and Technology” by the [[Korean Academy of Science and Technology]] (KAST).<ref name="KAST" /> He received major national honors in Korea, including the [[National Academy of Sciences Award (South Korea)|National Academy of Sciences Award]] (1961) and the [[Order of Civil Merit (South Korea)|Order of Civil Merit]] (Camellia, 1972; Rose of Sharon, 1997).<ref name="KAST" /> For context, the NAS Award is the principal academic prize of Korea’s National Academy of Sciences,<ref>{{cite web |title=The NAS Award – Overview |url=https://www.nas.go.kr/page/95ac2fed-4e4e-40f9-8cff-bd27248f97b6 |website=National Academy of Sciences (Republic of Korea) |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref> and the Order of Civil Merit is a presidential order of five grades, with ''Mugunghwa'' (Rose of Sharon) as the highest.<ref>{{cite web |title=훈장과 포장 (Orders and Medals) |url=https://www.sanghun.go.kr/nation/information/posangInfo3.do |website=대한민국 상훈 (Orders and Decorations of Korea) |language=ko |publisher=Ministry of the Interior and Safety |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
KSEA established the “Shoon Kyung Kim Scholarship” (2005) in his memory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shoon Kyung Kim Scholarship |url=https://award.ksea.org/scholarships/scholarships-for-undergraduates/shoon-kyung-kim-scholarship |website=KSEA |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
Kim died on 14 March 2003; he had been a professor at Temple University for 20 years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Shoon Kim Obituary |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=16 March 2003 |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/inquirer/name/shoon-kim-obituary?id=11628324 |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>
